records.citation: Westreich, P., Mimna, R., Brewer, J. (2020). The removal of short-chain and long-chain perfluoroalkyl acids and sulfonates via granular activated carbons: A comparative column study. Journal - American Water Works Association.

comparability.reason: Accessible information is limited to qualitative RSSCT column performance for PFAS in groundwater, with no numerical capacities, breakthrough criteria, bed volumes, or operating conditions; results are useful qualitatively (e.g., earlier PFBA breakthrough) but cannot be placed on a common quantitative basis with other studies or batch tests.

endpoints.interpretation: RSSCT column removal performance for a suite of long- and short-chain PFAS by GAC; effectiveness emphasized for PFAS with four or more perfluorinated carbons.

Comparative breakthrough of individual PFAS in GAC columns; PFBA exhibited much earlier breakthrough than all other PFAS tested, indicating lower effective capacity or weaker retention under column conditions.

limitations.statement: Only abstract-level information is available; RSSCT operating parameters (e.g., EBCT, bed depth, flow rate, influent PFAS concentrations) and breakthrough criteria are not reported in the accessible text, limiting quantitative interpretation and scale-up analysis.

The study uses a site-specific groundwater matrix, so co-contaminants and natural organic matter may influence PFAS removal and limit generalizability to other waters, but the abstract does not quantify these effects.
Only RSSCT column tests are described in the accessible abstract; there is no batch adsorption data available in this source to directly compare batch versus column performance for PFAS.

comparability.reason: The accessible content describes a modeling framework calibrated with pilot/RSSCT/full-scale column data but does not report specific operating conditions, breakthrough criteria, or quantitative performance metrics needed for comparison with batch or other systems.

endpoints.interpretation: Study demonstrates automated model fitting to pilot-column (or RSSCT/full-scale) PFAS breakthrough data and use of fitted parameters to predict column performance for a multi-PFAS treatment objective, while evaluating associated uncertainties.
endpoints.reported_term: model performance; breakthrough prediction; multi-PFAS treatment objective

endpoints.interpretation: Authors note that using pilot/RSSCT/full-scale data to estimate isotherm and transport parameters captures system-specific factors that control breakthrough but leaves greater uncertainty about the true isotherm parameters themselves.

limitations.statement: Using pilot, RSSCT, or full-scale column data as the basis for modeling PFAS breakthrough provides less certainty about the true isotherm parameters, even though it captures other system-specific factors that influence breakthrough.
